decisive_items: plate-like subepidermal tumor extending horizontally under epidermis with multiple cord-like connections to overlying epidermis
Neoplastic cords consisted of clear/pale epithelial cells with cytoplasm showing strong periodic acid-Schiff staining due to glycogen accumulation
Marked elastosis observed in dermis surrounding tumor
response.rationale: Histopathology shows a subepidermal tumor with clear glycogen-rich cells and cord-like connections, characteristic of eccrine poroma. Clinical hypopigmented macules and lack of hair growth are nonspecific; nevus depigmentosus lacks such tumor histology, and tuberous sclerosis has different lesions.

rejected.why: Clinical hypopigmented macules are nonspecific; no histologic or syndromic features of tuberous sclerosis (e.g., angiofibromas, shagreen patch) are provided.
Nevus depigmentosus is a congenital hypopigmented patch without the described subepidermal tumor or glycogen-rich clear cells on biopsy.
